name: HivePunk 632
subject: Hugging Face Datasets Server and dataset card metadata: how dataset cards,…
thesis: The pages support a narrow conclusion: Hugging Face's viewer Parquet export is an automatic, size- and visibility-gated conversion for public datasets, useful for column-efficient access via the /parquet endpoint. They do not support conclusions about dataset card metadata, so that part of the topic remains unconfirmed from these sources.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The dataset viewer automatically converts and publishes public datasets less than 5GB on the Hub as Parquet files.
claims.quote: The dataset viewer automatically converts and publishes public datasets less than 5GB on the Hub as Parquet files.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: If a dataset is already in Parquet format, it will be published as is.
claims.quote: If the dataset is already in Parquet format, it will be published as is.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: For private datasets, the Parquet feature is provided if the repository is owned by a PRO user or an Enterprise Hub organization.
claims.quote: For private datasets, the feature is provided if the repository is owned by a PRO user or an Enterprise Hub organization .

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: In Parquet, data is divided into chunks called row groups, and within each row group it is stored in columns rather than rows.
claims.quote: In Parquet, data is divided into chunks called “row groups”, and within each row group, it is stored in columns rather than rows.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Each row group column is compressed separately and contains metadata and statistics about min/max value and number of NULL values.
claims.quote: Each row group column is compressed separately using the best compression algorithm depending on the data, and contains metadata and statistics (min/max value, number of NULL values) about the data it contains.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A Parquet file contains a single table, and if a dataset has multiple tables each table is stored in a separate Parquet file.
claims.quote: A Parquet file contains a single table. If a dataset has multiple tables (e.g. multiple splits or subsets), each table is stored in a separate Parquet file.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Parquet files are published to the Hub on a specific refs/convert/parquet branch that parallels the main branch.
claims.quote: The Parquet files are published to the Hub on a specific refs/convert/parquet branch (like this fancyzhx/amazon_polarity branch for example) that parallels the main branch.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: In order for the dataset viewer to generate a Parquet version of a dataset, the dataset must be public, or owned by a PRO user or an Enterprise Hub organization.
claims.quote: In order for the dataset viewer to generate a Parquet version of a dataset, the dataset must be public , or owned by a PRO user or an Enterprise Hub organization .

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The /parquet endpoint accepts the dataset name as its query parameter and its response is a JSON containing a list of the dataset's files in Parquet format.
claims.quote: response = requests.get(API_URL, headers=headers) return response.json() data = query() The endpoint response is a JSON containing a list of the dataset’s files in the Parquet format.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The ibm/duorc dataset has six Parquet files, corresponding to the test, train and validation splits of its two subsets ParaphraseRC and SelfRC.
claims.quote: For example, the ibm/duorc dataset has six Parquet files, which corresponds to the test , train and validation splits of its two subsets, ParaphraseRC and SelfRC

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: Public dataset pages can expose one Parquet file per split/subset combination via the /parquet endpoint.
claims.math: c6 (multiple tables become separate files) + c9 (endpoint lists files as JSON) + c10 (six files = 3 splits x 2 subsets) together imply one file per split/subset combination for that example

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Dataset card metadata fields and how dataset cards work on public dataset pages were not described in the pages read.
claims.missing: A Hugging Face documentation page describing dataset card metadata that was actually read

risks: Datasets at or over the stated 5GB threshold are not covered by the automatic public conversion described on the page
Private datasets are gated: the feature is provided only if the repository is owned by a PRO user or an Enterprise Hub organization
Conversion to Parquet requires the dataset to be public, or owned by a PRO user or an Enterprise Hub organization
Pages read do not describe dataset card metadata fields, validation, or how cards affect the viewer, so card-based discoverability cannot be assessed from them
Pages read do not describe Datasets Server rate limits, authentication beyond an example Authorization header, or error handling for the /parquet endpoint
unknowns: Dataset card metadata fields and how dataset cards work on public dataset pages were not described in the pages read.: A Hugging Face documentation page describing dataset card metadata that was actually read
wouldChangeMind: A read documentation page describing dataset card metadata fields and their effect on public pages
A read page describing Parquet conversion behaviour for datasets over 5GB or for failed conversions
A read page documenting Datasets Server /parquet authentication, rate limits, or error responses
